clue.text: Beer a perk for this person? Could be

indicators.note: the closing 'Could be' hints that the letters of the opening words could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A pub worker wonders whether a free drink is one of the job's fringe benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' signals the anagram of BEER A PERK. 'for' is a link word, and 'this person' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in question is someone who serves drinks at a bar, for whom a beer might be a perk.

clue.text: Withdraw support given on course

parts.note: to back something is to support it
a track is a course for racing

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from backing a racecourse project.
explanation.definitionFit: To backtrack is to retreat from a position, the idiom for withdrawing a claim or commitment.

clue.text: Inn wrecked after Twickenham game results in arrest

parts.note: Twickenham is the London home of rugby union, abbreviated RU

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the letters of the word inn are smashed up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: After the rugby, the pub is trashed and the police step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' gives NIN, and 'after' sets it behind the game. Twickenham is England's national rugby stadium in south-west London; 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-in is an informal noun for an arrest or brush with the law, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Final broadcast at close of play

definitions.meaning: the closing programme of a broadcasting day, a short reflective piece on old BBC schedules
the speech or section that concludes a stage play

explanation.walkthrough: 'close of play' looks like cricket's end of the day's play, but here the play is a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the closing item of a day's transmissions and the concluding speech of a drama.

clue.text: American help organised to fill Physical Training brochure

indicators.note: to fill says the following abbreviation is packed around the other pieces
organised means the letters of help are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An American offers to help produce a fitness leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' gives PHLE; 'to fill' puts the American plus that inside the training abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet is a small booklet of information, much the same thing as a brochure.

clue.text: Stick to beat unpleasant person up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, puts the unpleasant person on top of the beat

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person
to tan someone is to thrash them

explanation.surface: Someone vows to give a nasty fellow a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'up' means placed higher, so the unpleasant person sits above the beating. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is a climbing palm whose stems are made into canes, so a rattan is a walking stick or cane.

clue.text: Youngster embracing popular film star?

indicators.note: embracing says one word is hugged inside the other

parts.note: a pup is a young animal, or a cheeky youngster
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A child hugs a celebrated cinema idol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts the popular word inside the youngster. The question mark flags that the definition is an example: a star's poster on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin-up is a picture of an attractive celebrity pinned to a wall, often a film star.

clue.text: Condition included by fleet to end fighting

indicators.note: included by says the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: fleet means fast, which is pacy
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A peace treaty contains a clause covering the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like ships but means swift. 'included by' puts the condition inside it; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify a region is to bring its fighting to a stop and restore peace.

clue.text: Criminal disrupted one US fair

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A felon causes chaos at an American funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' signals an anagram of ONE US FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or villainous, a synonym of criminal as an adjective.

clue.text: Holy group's guide

parts.note: PI is short for pious, holy
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A religious community has its own leader.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword staple for holy; the 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone who steers or guides, as a ship's pilot through a harbour.

clue.text: Lay hands on criminal joining organisation

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a firm is a business organisation

explanation.surface: A crook gets his hands on things after joining a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay hands on' looks like seizing, but refers to a bishop's touch in a church rite. 'joining' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rite of confirmation a bishop lays hands on each candidate, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Sensitive time to do something not quite sufficient

parts.note: to act is to do something

indicators.note: not quite says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: full can mean ample or sufficient

explanation.surface: A tactful soul warns that now is the moment to act, though there is barely enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' cuts the last L off FULL to leave FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tactful means being sensitive to other people's feelings.

clue.text: With style, execute work of art

parts.note: ton is fashionable style
to do a task is to execute it

explanation.surface: Someone stylishly produces a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: TON for style is old-fashioned, from the French for tone. 'With' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tondo is a circular painting or relief, a Renaissance form of artwork.

clue.text: Two principals meeting precipitately

parts.note: head and first both mean principal or chief
head and first both mean principal or chief

explanation.surface: Two headteachers have a hasty meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principals' looks like school heads, but gives two words meaning main. 'meeting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Going in headfirst means acting rashly, without thought, which is to act precipitately.

clue.text: Mail-order supplier?

parts.note: reads as a catalogue retailer, but the mail is chain mail, ordered from a maker of protective gear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mail-order' is a business model in the surface, but chain mail is the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: An armourer makes and supplies armour, including coats of chain mail.

clue.text: Equipment New Model Army got across ravine

indicators.note: got across says the rearranged word spans the ravine, holding it inside
New Model, as in Cromwell's army, says the letters of army are remodelled

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used in southern England

explanation.surface: Cromwell's soldiers haul their gear over a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Model' remodels the army as MARY, and 'got across' puts the ravine inside it after its second letter. A chine is a ravine, as on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery is mechanical equipment collectively.

clue.text: What does one play in game of cards?

definitions.meaning: a piece performed by a single player alone
a whist variant in which one player takes on the others

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word. The first definition reads as a question about cards, but means a performance by one musician.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an unaccompanied performance and a version of whist.

clue.text: Store wrong old information for body chemical

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of store are set out incorrectly

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A shop keeps out-of-date data about a hormone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns STORE into OESTR. 'for' is a link word; GEN is informal British for information.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hormone, a chemical messenger produced in the body.

clue.text: Home cover's got on sound credit

parts.note: a dome is a rounded cover, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: sound says the letters entered are what the slang word for credit sounds like

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Household insurance is bought on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' gives TIC, which is said like TICK (on tick means on credit in Britain). 'got on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic means relating to the home or household.

clue.text: One new, mostly healthy, worker needed a breathing aid

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: mostly says the word drops its last letter

parts.note: hale means healthy
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A new, fit employee has to use an inhaler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts HALE to HAL. 'needed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhalant is a medicine taken by breathing it in, helping the breathing.

clue.text: Thrill to get out of addiction

definitions.meaning: a buzz or rush of excitement
to give up a habit, as in the idiom about drugs or smoking

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden thrill and, as a verb, to give up a habit.

clue.text: Awkward customers consequently call for assistance outside

indicators.note: outside says the distress call surrounds the other phrase

parts.note: SOS is the distress call
and so means consequently

explanation.surface: Difficult clients therefore phone for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the distress call round the phrase for consequently, which goes in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-sos is a mild term for unpleasant or difficult people.

clue.text: Unit is deployed where it's stationed

indicators.note: deployed means the letters of unit is are moved into new positions

explanation.surface: An army unit is posted to its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' signals an anagram of UNIT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original place, where a thing is positioned.

clue.text: Sticky food — it's not used in expedition

indicators.note: is not used in says the word is dropped from inside the longer one

parts.note: expedition can mean speed, which is celerity
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gooey food was not part of the explorers' rations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' looks like a journey but means speed. 'it's not used in' removes IT. 'Sticky' points to a stick of the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The vegetable comes in long stalks, or sticks, and is eaten raw or cooked.

clue.text: Right to allow back into church people coming for service

indicators.note: into says the pieces go inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lien is a legal right over property

indicators.note: back says the word for allow is read in reverse

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A churchgoer has the right to be let back into the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LET into TEL; LIEN plus TEL goes 'into' CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clientele are a business's customers, those who come to it to be served.

clue.text: Officer in charge is a pain

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: The commanding officer is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Officer in charge' looks like one unit (OC or CO) but splits in two. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, especially in babies.

clue.text: One who's reckoned a total reptile

definitions.meaning: a person or machine that sums figures

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both someone who sums figures and a viper.

clue.text: Bride is marrying partly for religious belief

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wedding is partly a matter of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' signals the hidden run inside BriDE IS Marrying; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator god who does not intervene in the world.

clue.text: Confederates find shelter here

parts.note: the Confederates were Robert E. Lee's side in the American Civil War
the Confederates were Robert E. Lee's side in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: Southern soldiers look for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate army. 'find' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind is sheltered, so that is where sailors find shelter.

clue.text: Finding a Conservative in Herts town

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the town's name

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire

explanation.surface: A Tory is discovered in a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: TRING is a small town in Hertfordshire (Herts), north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing someone is tracking them down, so it is a finding as a verbal noun.

clue.text: Fur supplier shy about success

parts.note: coy means shy

indicators.note: about says the word for success is turned round

parts.note: up means on the rise, doing well

explanation.surface: A timid furrier is unsure of making it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a South American rodent farmed for its fur, called nutria.

clue.text: Belting out shanty, Mac is revealed as a sailor

indicators.note: belting out suggests the words are sung so loudly they are reshaped

explanation.surface: A Scot bellowing a sea song is shown to be a seafarer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belting out' signals the anagram of SHANTY MAC; 'is revealed as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yachtsman sails a yacht, a kind of sailor.
